3.0.0.en: Paul affirms that he does not need to commend himself to his disciples by what he offers them, nor does he need letters of recommendation to them or from them, as some preachers did, because he is known among them as an apostle, and his works among them bear witness to him.

3.1.0.en: Having declared that he has no need of letters of recommendation to the Corinthians, Paul offers the alternative, namely the believers in Corinth, and counts them as his epistle, which is not written on paper but in his heart, that is, he loves them and prays for them. On the other hand, this epistle, that is, the believers in Corinth, is visible before the believers of the other churches as proof of Paul's preaching. They are a living epistle that every person sees when he learns of the faith and strength of the Church of Corinth, especially since it is a city famous in the world.

3.2.0.en: Paul affirms that the believers in Corinth are an epistle from God to the whole world, and it was written through Paul's ministry and preaching among them.

3.2.1.en: This epistle differs from letters of recommendation in that the first is written by the work of the Holy Spirit in the believers, while the second is merely ink on paper. This epistle also differs from, and is more exalted than, God's message to His people in the Old Testament, which was the Ten Commandments written on two tables of stone, whereas Christ's epistle in the Church of Corinth is the fleshy hearts of the believers who live with God.

3.3.0.en: Paul does not need letters of recommendation for the Corinthians to trust him, but the faith of these believers in Corinth gives him confidence, through the power of Christ before God, that he is an apostle and a faithful servant.

3.4.0.en: After declaring that his preaching in Corinth is the proof of his apostleship, and is the letter of recommendation that confirms the success of his ministry and his sincerity, he declares that this ministry is by the power of God and not his own power; he is not sufficient in himself, but by the work of God.

3.4.1.en: Do you feel that you are responsible for ministering to those around you and for presenting Christ to them alive in your life and conduct? Do you care for them spiritually and bind them to the Church? Do you give them love and care for their needs?

3.4.2.en: This is your mission in life: to offer love and to care for everyone, especially those around you.

3.5.s.en: (2) The glory of the New Testament

3.5.0.en: It is Christ who made Paul and his companions sufficient for this ministry and able to perform it. The ministry of the New Testament is distinguished from the ministry of the Old Testament in that it shows the spiritual depths of the commandment and its effect on the person, whereas the Jews understood the commandments of the Old Testament literally and did not know their depths. Likewise, the commandments of the Old Testament exposed the sins of human beings and condemned them to its penalty, that is, death, whereas the ministry of the New Testament is what helped believers to carry out the commandments by the power of the Holy Spirit and gave them new life in Christ.

3.6.0.en: Engraven in stones: the Ten Commandments written on two tables of stone; here the whole Law is meant.

3.6.1.en: The Apostle Paul makes clear that the commandments of the Law, which condemned man to death because of his inability to fulfill them, were given by God in glory, in the form of the lightnings and thunders that occurred when Moses received them on the mountain (Ex 19:16). The people were greatly afraid of this great divine glory, and even more than this, after Moses met with God his face shone, and the children of Israel could not bear to see its radiance throughout his life, so he put a veil on his face when he spoke with them, and then took it off when he went in to stand before God in the tabernacle of the congregation (Ex 34:35).

3.7.0.en: The Apostle continues his comparison of the ministry of the New Testament with the old, declaring that if the latter was in glory, how much more glorious will the ministry of the New Testament be, in which the Holy Spirit works.

3.8.0.en: The Apostle affirms the greatness of the glory of the ministry of the New Testament over the old, in that he calls the latter the ministry of condemnation, because the commandments of the Old Testament condemn man and sentence him to death, whereas the ministry of the New Testament, in which the Holy Spirit works, forgives the believer's sins and justifies him, and therefore grants him greater glory.

3.9.0.en: That which was made glorious: that is, Christ. In this respect: it was not given glory like Moses. The glory that excelleth: the unlimited divine glory. The Apostle adds that Moses, the leader of the ministry of the Old Testament, whom God glorified before the eyes of the people, cannot be compared in glory with Christ, who has the glory that excels over all human beings, as was shown at the Transfiguration of Christ on the mountain, with a great radiance far greater than the splendor of Moses and Elijah. For Christ is God, of perfect and unlimited glory.

3.10.0.en: Moses is a transient man, and the ministry of the Law is limited, lasting 1,500 years, whereas the ministry of Christ, that is, the New Testament, is permanent forever, and therefore its glory is greater. The Church in the New Testament expresses the glory of this ministry by lighting lamps during the prayers even in the daytime, as well as lighting candles and lanterns, the priest's lifting the Gospel over his head, and the people's standing in reverence at the reading of the Gospel.

3.10.1.en: It is a great grace to live in the New Testament. May you enjoy partaking of the Holy Mysteries and meditating on the words of the Holy Bible, and so experience deep prayers with God that draw your heart to the glories of eternity.

3.11.s.en: (3) The revelation of God in the New Testament

3.11.0.en: Paul declares that he has hope and confidence in the ministry of the Gospel of the New Testament, because it is powerful and spiritual and has an excelling glory, for it depends on Christ. Therefore he speaks boldly in his preaching without fear.

3.12.0.en: Veil: a covering or a piece of cloth.

3.12.1.en: That which is abolished: the face of Moses, which would turn to dust in the grave and its glory pass away.

3.12.2.en: The old testament: the books of the Old Testament

3.12.3.en: Is done away in Christ: upon believing in Christ.

3.12.4.en: Moses is read: the five books of Moses.

3.12.5.en: It shall turn to the Lord: by repentance and faith in Christ.

3.12.6.en: Paul makes clear that the veil which Moses used to put on his face to hide its radiance when he spoke with the children of Israel signifies the hardness of the hearts of the Jews, which is like a veil on their hearts, so that it hides from them the words of the books of the Old Testament, which they hear in their synagogues and which prophesy about Christ. But when they believe in Christ and turn back from the hardness of their hearts, they will understand the prophecies.

3.13.2.en: The Apostle shows the work of the hypostases together in the New Testament. The one who believes in Christ has the Holy Spirit working in him, who is the Spirit of Christ, and when the Holy Spirit works in the believer He frees him from the condemnation of the Law upon him and gives him power and freedom to go forth in the love of God, so that he understands the commandments spiritually and not literally, and goes deeply into them and lives by them.

3.14.0.en: The face of the Lord: Christ.

3.14.1.en: A glass: the Holy Bible, the Sacraments, and the means of grace such as prayers, fasts, and so on.

3.14.2.en: We are changed: from human life to the spirituality of the children of God.

3.14.3.en: The image: man is the image of God and the image of Christ.

3.14.4.en: From glory to glory: spiritual growth in degrees toward perfection.

3.14.5.en: The Lord the Spirit: the Holy Spirit.

3.14.6.en: When we believe in Christ, we are gradually changed from our human ways to the exaltedness of the life of the children of God, because we see Christ through the Holy Bible, we are united with Him in the Holy Sacraments, and we come to know Him through prayers, fasts and service. Thus in the New Testament God reveals Himself to us the nearer we draw to Him through spiritual striving, and by this we advance in spiritual degrees toward holiness by the power of the work of the Holy Spirit in us.

3.14.7.en: This spiritual growth will continue in eternity, so that God is revealed to us and we see Him face to face in a great revelation and not as in a glass (a limitation), and we keep discovering His love and His depths and delighting in them forever.

3.14.8.en: Today you have come into the glory of the New Testament, and you have come to see Christ and touch Him.

3.14.9.en: Has this relationship helped you to change, so that everyone who deals with you sees this glory that you have received from God, and notices this change in you?

3.14.10.en: God took a bodily form different from His nature in order to change us and make us in the image of His glory and splendor. So we must walk in purity and righteousness, and people will see our good works and glorify our Father who is in heaven.

3.14.11.en: God's blessings to His suffering servants

4.0.0.en: Therefore: because of the excelling glory of the ministry of the New Testament over the ministry of the Old Testament, that is, the Law.

4.0.1.en: This ministry: the ministry of preaching the Gospel.

4.0.2.en: As we have received mercy: God turned Paul from serving the Law and persecuting the Christians to preaching the Gospel, and this is a great divine mercy.

4.0.3.en: We faint not: we do not stumble and become negligent in preaching, and so become unfaithful or failing servants. The Apostle Paul feels the greatness of the ministry of the New Testament, indeed he sees it as a great grace and mercy from God that He allows him to be His servant. Therefore he holds fast to it and performs it faithfully and does not become idle or fall short in it.

4.1.0.en: The hidden things of dishonesty: shameful sins that a person is ashamed to have appear before others.

4.1.1.en: Craftiness: twisting words to achieve personal ends, as the scribes and Pharisees did with Christ.

4.1.2.en: Handling the word of God deceitfully: interpreting it according to personal purposes, or showing what pleases people and hiding what troubles them in order to win their love.

4.1.3.en: Commending ourselves: sound conduct that God approves through the pure conscience of people. In the sight of God: Paul always feels the presence of God, so he walks uprightly because God sees him.

4.1.4.en: After Paul felt the greatness of the ministry of preaching the Gospel, he took care for the purity of his heart and the uprightness of his conduct in his preaching, so as to proclaim the divine truth as God wishes and not according to his personal purposes. By this he is accepted by God, and even commended by the pure consciences of people. Thus he wins God's mercy and the hearts of his hearers.

4.2.0.en: Hid: its glory, power and effect not clear.

4.2.1.en: Them that are lost: those who walk in sins, so they refuse to believe in the Gospel and eternal destruction awaits them. The Apostle declares that the preaching of the Gospel does not reach all people, although it is powerful and effective in any ordinary person, but it becomes obscure and rejected by those who walk in evil, who reject the word of God because it opposes their personal purposes.

4.3.0.en: The god of this world: Satan.

4.3.1.en: The light of the glorious Gospel of Christ: the Gospel teaches us the truth and lifts us out of shameful sins so that we become children of God and know God and love Him.

4.3.2.en: The image of God: by the Incarnation of Christ He showed us the perfect image of God, so that human beings might follow His example and restore the image of God that was disfigured in them.

4.3.3.en: The reason the Gospel is hidden and obscure to those who are lost is that Satan has occupied them with sin, so they have become blind and do not see the greatness of the Gospel, and even refuse to be enlightened by its knowledge because it exposes their sins. This Gospel is the Word of God, the incarnate Christ, by whom God reveals Himself to us in a life lived among us, so that we may learn from Him and walk in the truth.

4.4.0.en: The aim of Paul's preaching is to persuade people that Christ is God, their Savior and Redeemer, and he has no personal purposes, for he does not glorify himself. And if the only aim of the preaching is the glorification of Christ, Paul counts himself a bondservant consecrated to serving the Corinthians so that they may believe in Christ.

4.5.0.en: St. Paul affirms that the preaching of the Gospel depends on the power of God. Just as God created light on the first day when the whole world was darkness, He also enlightens our hearts in the New Testament, and shines upon us, not with a material sun but with His Holy Spirit, that we may know God and recover our sonship to Him and be glorified in Him by this knowledge. This is through the visible image of God, that is, the incarnate Christ, in whom we have seen and from whom we learn the ability to fulfill the commandment, and we touch Him closely through the Holy Bible and the Sacraments of the Church, and are even united with Him, so that we experience His great glory in us.

4.5.1.en: God enlightens our life in the Church by His Holy Sacraments and His spiritual word. May we go deeper every day and increase in prayers and readings so that we may enjoy knowing Him, and it may appear in our conduct, and we may call many to know Him and be joined to Him.

4.6.0.en: The treasure: the knowledge of Christ and preaching Him.

4.6.1.en: Earthen vessels: he likens himself and all the servants to weak vessels like pottery, but the greatness is in what fills them, that is, what they preach, which is the Gospel.

4.6.2.en: The Apostle shows that the power working in the ministry is the power of God, which is not hindered by the weakness of the servants, and this calls us to thank God, the source of power in the preaching, and not the gifts or abilities of the servants.

4.7.0.en: Paul shows his weaknesses and those of the other servants during the preaching. Problems and obstacles meet them that cause them some depression because of their weakness as human beings, but the power of God does not leave them, so they do not give up but continue their ministry with zeal and persistence, enduring troubles and sufferings with thanksgiving.

4.7.1.en: For the devil, in his wars with the servants, makes them perplexed about the means by which they serve, because he opposes them and sometimes succeeds in hindering their means, but they do not despair; rather they rise again and continue the service by new means and with other people, by the power of God.

4.8.0.en: The devil stirs up various persecutions against the servants, and they endure them because God does not leave them but supports and encourages them, so they count the sufferings of the ministry a sharing in the cross of Christ and a crown of glory for Him. The devil prevails against them and makes them fall into sin, or shows their physical weakness before the wicked, but God strengthens them and heals them and raises them up again with power, so that they continue their striving and their ministry.

4.9.0.en: The dying of the Lord Jesus: the sufferings that the servants endure, which almost cost them their lives.

4.9.1.en: Always delivered unto death: we are continually exposed to death through persecutions.

4.9.2.en: Our mortal flesh: the weak body, liable and exposed to death.

4.9.3.en: In sum, the Apostles and servants of Christ are always ready to endure sufferings for Christ, and even control the desires of the body and its comfort and strive in worship and service, enduring every labor. Then the grace of God and His power are manifested, as He supports these weak bodies and works through them. And in proportion to the servant's surrender of his life to God and his acceptance of sufferings, he experiences the grace of God in him and feels His fellowship, and even receives the pledge of the Kingdom while on earth in inexpressible spiritual feelings. That is, God turns affliction into a blessing, and persecutions and labors become an opportunity to see God and to be with Him.

4.10.0.en: What appears in the Apostles and servants is the endurance of sufferings and persecutions and constant exposure to death, and these sufferings are even counted as a partial death. When the believers see the steadfastness of the servants and the power of God's word in them, they hold fast to God in spiritual striving and experience new depths in life with Him.

4.11.0.en: The sufferings that St. Paul met in his ministry did not hinder him from continuing to preach, because he believes in Christ, who strengthens him, just as David believed in ancient times and endured sufferings and persecutions and proclaimed the truth (Ps 116:10). Since Paul enjoys the same faith, he continues his preaching despite the persecutions.

4.11.1.en: "I believed, therefore have I spoken." Beloved brother, this blessed verse places all of us before a great responsibility. Faith by its nature is not mute, and Christianity spread by the preaching of the Apostles and of everyone who believed as well. So we must make our conversations and words express our faith, and if society prevents us from speaking our faith, then let our deeds speak and bear witness to our God.

4.12.0.en: Shall present us with you: we shall all meet in the Kingdom around Christ.

4.12.1.en: Paul takes courage in enduring sufferings by looking to the glories of eternity, and he declares his faith in the final resurrection. Just as God raised up the Lord Jesus from the dead, that is, raised Christ Himself, He will also raise us up on the last day and set us with Him in the Kingdom, to be glorified with Him in return for all our labors on earth. This in turn urges us to continue striving and serving.

4.13.0.en: All things: the Apostles' endurance of sufferings and the work of God's grace in them.

4.13.1.en: St. Paul sees that all the persecutions and sufferings that happen to him are permitted by God not only for his benefit, but also for all those to whom he preaches in Corinth, so that their faith may be confirmed and they may offer prayers for him. Thus God's grace abounds toward him through the prayers of many of the believers of Corinth, which moves him and the whole Church of Corinth to give thanks to God, and God is glorified in them.

4.13.2.en: Do you feel that every pain and trial you endure with thanksgiving and without complaint gives glory to God? Then accept it and ask for God's help, confident that this turns into a spiritual blessing in your life and glories in heaven.

4.14.2.en: He welcomes sufferings for their benefits. Even if the body is exposed to many sufferings from persecutions and the abuse of others, this does not make us feel failure in our service, because it benefits us spiritually: the spirit is bound to God through every affliction, and the person's feelings are renewed in a deeper relationship that makes him grow spiritually throughout the days of his life, through prayers and the experience of relying on God and His work within us, so we feel a spiritual fellowship and enjoy God.

4.15.0.en: Paul sees that the afflictions to which he is exposed are light and small compared with the glory he will receive in the Kingdom, which will be great, or "weighty," as he expresses it against the lightness of the affliction. On the other hand, the affliction is temporary and takes a limited time in this life, whereas the glories of the Kingdom continue forever. Indeed he encourages us that the more afflictions we endure, the more glories we receive in heaven, and these afflictions are small and limited while the glories are great and eternal.

4.16.0.en: The things which are seen: all the material things in the world.

4.16.1.en: The things which are not seen: spiritual matters and our relationship with God.

4.16.2.en: From what has gone before, the Apostle concludes how we should walk in life: we should not be concerned about earthly things if we lose them and are exposed to bodily sufferings, because all this is temporary, but let us care for our spiritual life, for it extends forever.

4.16.3.en: Do not be troubled if you lose some material things or are exposed to abuse from those around you. All these things are transient, but try to take refuge in God and seize opportunities to be with Him, so that you enjoy His fellowship and prepare your heart for the eternal Kingdom.

4.16.4.en: Preparing for eternity and calling people to reconciliation with God
